title: Groups call shutdown and march in Kargil over election timing

tea.why: Protesters fear that holding local elections in winter will disenfranchise nearly 25% of the population who migrate away from the region.
tea.want: Deferment of the upcoming local elections to April or May next year.
tea.changed: Nov 10: Kargil observed a complete shutdown and scheduled an evening candlelight march.

summary: Political parties, religious groups, and civil society organisations in Kargil called for a complete shutdown and a candlelight march on Tuesday to protest against the timing of upcoming local elections. Organisers, including leaders from the Kargil Democratic Alliance, argued that holding polls in the winter season would disenfranchise approximately a quarter of Ladakh's population, including students, the elderly, and members of the business community, who migrate outside the region during harsh weather conditions. Leaders also criticized the administration for imposing decisions without consulting local stakeholders. The Lieutenant Governor administration has not formally commented on the specific protests, though officials noted that municipal and panchayat elections were scheduled to take place in November.
demands: Postpone panchayat and municipal elections to April or May
Consult local stakeholders on electoral decisions
response: No official response reported in the sources regarding the shutdown, though officials noted the election schedule was set to be completed before November 30.

updates.text: Political and religious groups in Kargil organized a complete shutdown and a planned evening candlelight march.
